items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: And one of the help got Johnny McGovern, who was a tough Irish kid.

ctx.x: Now, one of the funniest things there was Totts Scott, a piano player and a very fine one. Well, at that time, Roosevelt came in with the Blue Eagle thing. Now, that we should not be unfair to labor and all that. And the Liberty Inn was not that organized, anyway. They were very much against it. And one night, Tut got out -- whatever Rosicrucian or Far Eastern kick he was on, and decided to make a speech. And he told the drummer, give me a roll of the drums.

The drummer gave him a roll, and he upped and made this speech. And one of the help got Johnny McGovern, who was a tough Irish kid. And we're standing there listening to this guy talk, telling the people not to come in and go away, they were unfair and all that. And he's ready to kill this guy. And McGovern says, don't kill him, shake him. I never seen anything like that. He picked Tut up and just shook him, and shook all that nonsense out of him.

Now, previous to that, Tut was on a backward kick. He would walk into the Liberty Inn backwards. He would -- can you imagine walking into a tough place like that, where people are having an eye-opener and all that, back in through the bar, through the door that leads to the back room, back in, hang up your coat, back --
